analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation-only YAML comment block added to docs/threat-model.yaml at head lines 41-48, a 'SDK 27.2 Date comparison review 2026-11-04' note. It sits in the header comment area and does not alter any threat, asset, boundary, mitigation or status field. I checked the base excerpts (T-043..T-061, base lines 1846-2496) and the head excerpt (lines 1-473). Apart from the new comment, the head text matches the base, and no threat entries or mitigation statuses are changed or weakened.

The comment says App Attest Date comparisons (key-generation budget, enrollment resume, stall restart, key history) now use timeIntervalSince(_:) rather than >= / <=, because SDK 27.2 back-deploys those operators as weak imports that pre-release macOS 27.2 lacks. It says a call through one crashed the provider in a loop, and that thresholds and results are unchanged. It also says release builds refuse binaries importing either symbol, via scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py.

I can't verify these code claims because the source changes, the script and the Swift files are not in the supplied units. The comment attributes the issue to A-018 availability, which fits the asset's definition (provider serving availability). The comment does not claim to revalidate older entries, so it overclaims nothing about trust. The next pass should confirm that the code change preserves the budget and rate-limit semantics. In particular, the App Attest key-generation budget and enrollment-resume thresholds must remain equivalent at boundary equality, because they bound key churn relevant to T-055/T-057. It should also confirm that the weak-import check script is wired into release CI. This is unverified contract context, not a finding. No security regression is identified in the documentation change.
